builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Adaptive Quantization Preserves Fast Rates for TD Learning over Rate-Limited Channels
summary: BAQ-TD replaces uncompressed transmission of TD update directions from a reinforcement-learning agent to a server with batched, adaptively quantized innovations over a finite-capacity channel. The cost is added algorithmic complexity (batching plus an adaptive quantizer) and a minimum channel-capacity threshold below which the fast rate is not guaranteed. It can fail if the channel capacity falls below the proven threshold, if the linear function approximation assumption is violated, or if the theoretical setting (single-agent policy evaluation) does not match the deployment.
rationale: The method addresses communication-constrained distributed reinforcement learning, a setting unrelated to the reader's LLM inference and production constraints, and its results are theoretical rather than an adoptable engineering artifact.
technique: Adaptive quantized TD learning over rate-limited channels

claims.statement: BAQ-TD replaces uncompressed transmission of TD update directions from a reinforcement-learning agent to a server with batched, adaptively quantized innovations over a finite-capacity channel. The cost is added algorithmic complexity (batching plus an adaptive quantizer) and a minimum channel-capacity threshold below which the fast rate is not guaranteed. It can fail if the channel capacity falls below the proven threshold, if the linear function approximation assumption is violated, or if the theoretical setting (single-agent policy evaluation) does not match the deployment.

Transmitting O(d log(T)) bits over horizon T suffices to achieve the order-optimal O~(1/T) rate of unquantized TD, an exponential communication-complexity improvement over prior work (theoretical bound, no empirical factor reported).
